newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade at standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade at standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade near midday Monday was at a standstill, with no sales expected until midweek, feedlot sources said.
Light bids at $66.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle at $69.00, several sources said.
Most of last week's active cattle sales were done at $67.00, although there were light sales Wednesday at $68.00.
Packers reportedly bought enough cattle to cover needs through this week, which suggested they would not be in the market until Wednesday or Thursday, cattle feeders said.
Higher beef prices last week fueled projections for firm fed cattle prices this week, with some feedlot sources anticipating trade at $68.00 or higher.
The price of heavier-weight choice-grade beef rose $2.22 to $104.15 per cwt over the course of last week, USDA said.
Cattle showlists last week were mostly depleted which lent further credence to this week's price outlook. Feedlots remain extremely current in their marketings, sources said.
This week's showlists were said to be steady to slightly greater than last week, but were not expected to weigh on prices because of projections for strong packer demand.
